A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core algorithms, theory, and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated material and new additions.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original optimization experiments on synthetic distributions and Bayesian inference results for breast_cancer, wine, Boston, and MNIST.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds shared-variance comparisons, a repeated uniform-weight bias experiment, and MNIST comparisons with Laplace approximations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the core IBW and MD updates remain unchanged, as does the existing MNIST mean-field adaptation. v2 introduces IBW-s and MD-s variants that optimize one variance shared across components, a limited procedural extension used in the comparisons.

E1.justification: New Appendix E.4 evaluates a two-dimensional bimodal target with weights 0.1 and 0.9, extending the existing unequal-weight Gaussian-mixture scenarios. The real datasets, inference tasks, Funnel and heavy-tailed targets, and high-dimensional mixture coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands comparisons through IBW-s and MD-s in Figure 1 and the component visualizations, plus diagonal and K-FAC Laplace approximations on MNIST in Figure 13. The original comparator suite remains; the new explanation of missing MNIST HMC/ADVI results does not remove previously plotted comparisons.

E3.justification: New E.4 introduces mode-proportional initialization, 10,000 samples per distribution, and K-means location/weight error metrics. The MNIST study adds N=1 versus N=5 controls and PCA. Existing splits and Table 1 budgets remain. v2's new 'standard Gaussian prior' wording conflicts with retained non-unit prior variances, leaving any actual prior change unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial targeted analyses: shared versus component-specific variance ablations, component visualizations on existing targets, a component-count sweep testing uniform-weight approximation bias, and MNIST single-component controls with PCA examining component collapse. These directly investigate modeling choices beyond the retained benchmark evaluations.

E5.justification: Appendix E.4 newly specifies 10 repetitions and reports averages with error bars for the bias experiment. v1 contains no corresponding run-count statement. This does not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments, and v2 does not specify whether the bars represent standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the shared-variance comparisons, decreasing location/proportion errors with increasing N in Figure 8, and MNIST comparisons in Figure 13. The latter shows N=5 outperforming both Laplace baselines in final test accuracy, whereas N=1 remains below K-FAC. Most original benchmark plots are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix D corrects the squared Hellinger-distance definition from the affinity integral to one minus that integral, fixing its consistency with the proof. The original approximation bound and principal theoretical results remain. Appendix E.6.1 also adds the standard Taylor/Hessian derivation of Laplace approximation.

C1.justification: The abstract and central introduction/conclusion claims retain the same scope: efficient uniform-weight isotropic Gaussian-mixture VI using gradient updates for means and Bures or entropic updates for variances. The revised 'compelling balance' wording and additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how additional components compensate for uniform weights, interprets separate variances as improving adaptation to target shape, and links the MNIST findings to multimodal posterior representations. It also explicitly acknowledges unsuccessful HMC/ADVI tuning on MNIST. These extend the interpretation while retaining the existing Funnel limitation and main conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code URL for the RealNVP implementation, concrete initialization and sampling details for the bias study, and descriptions of diagonal/K-FAC Hessian approximations. The main VI-MIG code link, hardware information, and original hyperparameter table were already present in v1; moving the code link does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: v2 adds Izmailov et al. on Bayesian neural-network posteriors and Ritter et al. on scalable Laplace approximation, and explicitly attributes Appendix D's supporting lemmas to Huix et al. The overall positioning remains stable. The RealNVP reference's 2016-to-2017 update represents the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections and explanatory rewrites, numbers the conclusion as Section 7, and reorganizes Appendix E around the added bias and Laplace studies. The main narrative and theoretical appendix structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially: Figure 1 gains shared-variance curves, and new Figures 7, 8, and 13 show component geometry, approximation bias, and MNIST accuracy/PCA comparisons. Existing figures are also relocated or renumbered. The retained Bayesian-results panel changes its KL labels to ELBO without an evident numerical transformation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new ablations, repeated bias study, and MNIST Laplace comparison provide useful targeted support for the modeling choices, while the Hellinger correction improves mathematical consistency. The gains are limited by mode-informed initialization in the bias study and incomplete Laplace experimental settings. New inconsistencies, including the prior wording versus Table 1 and the unchanged loss curves relabeled ELBO, partly offset the improvements.
